provenance.inputs_seen_by_extractor: this evaluation's body text only (no paper, no model output)

issues.text: The model uses predictors measured contemporaneously with the outcome period (2000–2012/2016), such as net primary production, burned area, and road density, so predictions are conditional on events concurrent with regrowth. When applied to predict future regrowth, the model effectively assumes future predictor values that are unobserved, and the reported accuracy metrics therefore likely overstate true predictive performance.
issues.quote: Due to this temporal overlap, the predicted regrowth probabilities are conditional on events that are contemporaneous with the outcome. As a result, the model predicts the present rather than the future.

issues.text: Assumptions about future values of predictors closely tied to regrowth (net primary production, burned area, road density) are not reflected in the model accuracy metrics, so prediction error from these assumptions is non-quantified and likely spatially non-uniform.
issues.quote: Importantly, these assumptions are not reflected in the model accuracy metrics. The reported model accuracy thus likely overstates the true predictive performance.

issues.text: The spatial predictions are derived from a model using only biophysical predictors, but biophysical and socioeconomic conditions are interconnected, so the predictions reflect a joint outcome and cannot identify pure biophysical potential as the authors claim.
issues.quote: inferring purely biophysical potential from observational data is not feasible with the proposed method.

issues.text: Because socioeconomic factors suppress regeneration in some areas, the 215 Mha estimate is likely a lower bound on biophysical potential; the evaluator believes the figure is inaccurate and that the authors' interpretation of it is contrary to the evidence.
issues.quote: socioeconomic factors substantially influence this result. If socioeconomic factors were to be moderated, biophysical conditions could likely support a substantially larger area for natural regeneration.

issues.text: The evaluator has low confidence in the 215 Mha figure as an accurate biophysical potential estimate and notes that the spatial distribution of results is biased toward regions with low anthropogenic disturbance.
issues.quote: I have low confidence in the estimated 215 Mha being an accurate figure on biophysical potential.

issues.text: The study does not address regrowth longevity: the outcome only captures patches persisting to 2016, so very short-lived regeneration (under four years) is excluded and differences in persistence across regions are not captured, misdirecting targeting priorities.
issues.quote: The outcome data of the analysis do not identify locations with very short-lived forest regeneration lasting less than four years.

issues.text: The method ignores concurrent deforestation and annual forest-cover change data that could indicate which regrowth is likely to persist; the authors could use these data to differentiate regions by persistence.
issues.quote: one could differentiate between regions based on the degree of deforestation that is concurrent with forest regrowth in the same region.

issues.text: The predictions represent business-as-usual regeneration probability, so the regions highlighted are those where interventions would have the lowest additionality; the policy implication that these are priority areas for restoration is not supported without considering additionality.
issues.quote: The regions highlighted by the model are precisely those where interventions facilitating forest regrowth will have the lowest additionality.

issues.text: Opportunity costs of restoration are not considered, and there is no clear prior on their correlation with predicted regeneration probability, so the targeting advice may be misleading if used in isolation.
issues.quote: there is no clear empirical prior on whether they will be correlated with the prediction.

issues.text: The authors' policy claim that the model identifies areas where intervention effort and cost will be lowest and success highest is not reliable in isolation; the evaluator argues that the results alone should not guide policy choices.
issues.quote: these results alone should not guide policy choices.

issues.text: The predictions likely contain false negatives because anthropogenic factors mask high-potential areas, so the results are partial and in some cases biased or misleading guidance for policymakers.
issues.quote: The model predictions can provide only partial, and in some cases biased or even misleading guidance.
